home.metaTitle: Hec Sánchez | Product Engineer & Fractional CTO
home.metaDescription: I build software and help agencies and founders make better technical decisions. Explore my projects, writing, and ways to work together.
home.h1: I build software and help teams make better technical decisions.
intro: I'm Hec Sánchez, a product engineer and fractional CTO based in Puebla, Mexico. I have 16 years of experience building software, from customer-facing products to the systems businesses use every day.
I work with agencies and founders on product development, integrations, and technical leadership. Here, I share what I build and what I learn along the way.
home.workIntro: Products and business systems I've built, with a particular interest in the technology behind sales, marketing, and customer communication.
home.agenciesBody: Bring me into a client project that needs custom software, integrations, or experienced technical direction. I help define the work and build the parts your team needs to deliver.
home.foundersBody: Get help deciding what to build, improving an existing product, or leading the engineering work. We can start with a focused problem and shape the engagement around what your business needs.
home.writingIntro: Notes on building products, making technical decisions, and learning to run a business. Written from the work itself: the choices, mistakes, and questions that stay with me.

agencies.metaTitle: Custom Software & Integrations for Agencies | Hec Sánchez
agencies.metaDescription: Technical partnership for agencies delivering custom software, CRM integrations, HubSpot apps, and WhatsApp workflows. Work directly with Hec Sánchez.
agencies.serviceName: Custom software and integrations for agencies
agencies.h1: Custom software and integrations for agencies.
intro: I help digital, marketing, and product agencies deliver client work that needs experienced engineering. That includes CRM integrations, HubSpot apps, WhatsApp workflows, and custom software.
Bring me in to help define the technical scope, make the architecture decisions, and build the system. You work directly with me from the first conversation through the agreed delivery.
agencies.situationsTitle: When a client project needs more engineering
situations: Your client needs something beyond the existing tools. The CRM has to exchange data with another system. A campaign depends on a custom workflow. A product needs a feature your current team cannot take on.
I can help you work through the technical questions before you commit to a solution, then take responsibility for the agreed implementation.
agencies.servicesTitle: What I can help you deliver

services.title: CRM and business-system integrations
services.body: Connect the systems your clients use to capture leads, manage customers, and run their operations. Define how information moves between them, what happens when something fails, and how the team will maintain the integration.

services.title: HubSpot apps and sales workflows
services.body: Extend HubSpot with custom applications and integrations. Examples include lead assignment, agent availability, and connections to other sales tools.

services.title: WhatsApp workflows
services.body: Build WhatsApp into a product or business process, from authentication to customer communication. Choose an approach that fits the use case and the systems already in place.

services.title: Custom software and technical delivery
services.body: Build client portals, internal applications, and product features. I can also help with technical discovery, architecture reviews, and implementation planning when a project needs clearer direction.

work.body: A custom CRM I built for The Woods, a business selling wooden floors and materials.
A HubSpot application I built to assign leads using agent schedules, with a calendar view of availability.
A product I built for authentication through WhatsApp, using one-time codes and magic links.

process.title: Understand the client problem
process.body: We discuss what the client needs, the systems involved, the deadline, and your team's role. If the brief is still taking shape, we identify the decisions that need to be made first.

process.title: Agree the scope
process.body: I propose an engagement with clear deliverables, responsibilities, and a way to assess completion. That might be a technical assessment, a scoped implementation, or ongoing support.

process.title: Build and hand over
process.body: I implement the agreed work, keep you informed of progress and tradeoffs, and document what your team needs to operate or extend it.

faq.q: Can you work with our existing developers?
faq.a: Yes. I can take responsibility for a defined part of the project or work alongside your developers on architecture and implementation. We agree who owns each decision and deliverable at the start.

faq.q: Will you work directly with our client?
faq.a: We can agree how I participate before the engagement starts. That may mean working through your team or joining client conversations when technical input is useful.

faq.q: Do we need an ongoing retainer?
faq.a: A defined project can start as a scoped engagement. Ongoing support makes sense when there is a continuing need for engineering or technical leadership.

faq.q: What should we bring to the first call?
faq.a: A short description of the client problem, the current tools or product, any deadlines, and what you would like me to own. An unfinished brief is fine; we can identify the missing pieces together.

agencies.finalCtaTitle: Have a client project in mind?
agencies.finalCtaBody: Tell me what your client needs and where your team could use engineering support. We can use the first call to see whether there is a useful fit.

founders.metaTitle: Fractional CTO & Product Engineering | Hec Sánchez
founders.metaDescription: Product engineering and fractional CTO support for founders. Get help with architecture, implementation, and engineering leadership from Hec Sánchez.
founders.serviceName: Product engineering and fractional CTO support for founders
founders.h1: Technical direction and hands-on engineering for founders.
intro: I help founders make product and engineering decisions, build software, and give their teams clearer technical direction. Depending on what you need, I can work on a defined implementation or provide ongoing fractional CTO support.
My work combines product development with architecture and engineering leadership. I stay close to the code and the business problem it needs to solve.
situations: You have a product, but technical decisions keep landing on you without a clear way to evaluate them.
Your team is building, but priorities, architecture, or responsibilities need attention.
A feature or integration needs experienced implementation.
You need to assess an existing codebase before committing to the next stage of development.
You need someone to take ongoing responsibility for technical direction while the business grows.
founders.servicesTitle: The work we can do together

services.title: Decide what to build and how
services.body: Translate the business goal into a practical technical plan. Review the product, identify constraints, and weigh the tradeoffs between building, buying, and simplifying.

services.title: Build or improve your product
services.body: Take a defined part of the product through implementation. That could be a new feature, an integration, or an improvement to an existing system that is making delivery difficult.

services.title: Establish stronger engineering practices
services.body: Improve how the team plans work, reviews code, ships changes, and understands production issues. Focus on the practices that address the team's actual problems.

services.title: Provide ongoing technical leadership
services.body: As a fractional CTO, I can help own the technical roadmap, guide architecture, support hiring decisions, and work with the team as priorities change. We define the responsibility and time commitment around the business.

founders.workTitle: Products I've built and work I'm doing

work.body: I built Zaplink to support authentication through WhatsApp, including one-time codes and magic links.
I'm building technology for real estate sales operations, bringing product development into the day-to-day problems of sales teams.
I built a custom CRM for a business selling wooden floors and materials.

founders.engagementsTitle: Choose the engagement around the problem

engagements.label: Technical assessment
engagements.body: Understand the current system, identify risks, and leave with prioritized recommendations for what to do next.

engagements.label: Scoped implementation
engagements.body: Agree a specific outcome and the work needed to deliver it.

engagements.label: Fractional CTO support
engagements.body: Establish ongoing technical ownership when the business needs sustained direction across product, architecture, and the engineering team.

faq.q: Do I need a fractional CTO or a senior engineer?
faq.a: If the problem is a defined piece of implementation, an experienced engineer may be enough. A fractional CTO is useful when someone also needs to own ongoing technical priorities, architecture decisions, and the way the team operates.

faq.q: Can you work with my existing team or development partner?
faq.a: Yes. We can define an engagement that complements the people already doing the work, with clear responsibilities and communication.
Yes. Implementation is part of my work. The balance between coding and leadership depends on the engagement we agree.

faq.q: Can we start with an assessment?
faq.a: Yes. An assessment can be a useful first step when we need to understand the product or codebase before choosing the implementation work.

founders.finalCtaTitle: What does your product need next?
founders.finalCtaBody: Tell me what you are building, what is getting difficult, and which decisions you need help making.

about.metaTitle: About Hec Sánchez | Software Builder & Technical Leader
about.metaDescription: Meet Hec Sánchez, a product engineer and fractional CTO in Puebla, Mexico, with 16 years of experience building software and leading engineering work.
intro: I'm a product engineer and technical leader based in Puebla, Mexico. I've spent 16 years building software, and I still enjoy taking a problem apart, deciding what matters, and turning it into something people can use.

My work includes customer-facing products, custom business systems, integrations, and engineering leadership. I've contributed to software for organizations including Camino Real, Lala, Cabify, and Freightliner.
building: I built Zaplink, a product for authentication through WhatsApp. I'm also building technology for Estateflow, focused on real estate sales operations.
Other work includes a custom CRM for The Woods and a HubSpot application for assigning leads using agent schedules.
approach: I want to understand the business problem before deciding what software to build. Sometimes the useful work is a new application. Sometimes it is connecting existing tools, simplifying a process, or giving a team clearer technical direction.
I work across product decisions, architecture, and implementation. I care about software that people can use, teams can maintain, and businesses can continue to develop.
writing: I share observations from building products and working with teams: decisions that proved useful, mistakes I would handle differently, and ideas I want to understand better.
about.workWithMeBody: I work with agencies and founders in English and Spanish. We can start with a defined technical problem or discuss a longer-term need for engineering leadership.

howIWork.metaDescription: How Hec Sánchez approaches technical assessments, scoped software implementation, and ongoing engineering or fractional CTO engagements.
howIWork.h1: Start with the problem. Agree the work. Build from there.
howIWork.intro: I work directly with agencies and founders on software development and technical leadership. The right engagement depends on the problem, the people already involved, and the responsibility you need me to take.

ways.title: Technical assessment
ways.body: For situations where the next step is unclear. I review the relevant product, codebase, architecture, or workflow and identify the risks and decisions that matter. The deliverable is an assessment with prioritized recommendations.

ways.title: Scoped implementation
ways.body: For a defined feature, integration, application, or improvement. We agree what is included, who is responsible for dependencies, how progress will be reviewed, and what completion looks like.

ways.title: Ongoing technical support
ways.body: For work that needs continuing engineering or leadership. This can include architecture decisions, implementation, team support, or a fractional CTO role. We define the time allocation and responsibilities in the proposal.

process.label: Initial conversation.
process.body: Understand the business goal, current situation, and constraints.

process.label: Proposal.
process.body: Agree the scope, deliverables, responsibilities, timing, and fee before starting.

process.label: Delivery.
process.body: Work through the agreed priorities, share progress, and surface decisions or scope changes as they arise.

process.label: Handover or continuation.
process.body: Document the delivered work and agree whether there is a useful next engagement.

howIWork.routeBody: Agencies can bring me into client delivery. Founders can engage me for product engineering or ongoing technical direction.

fractionalCto.metaTitle: What Is a Fractional CTO? | Hec Sánchez
fractionalCto.metaDescription: Learn what a fractional CTO does, when ongoing technical leadership is useful, and how the role differs from a senior engineer or project consultant.
intro: A fractional CTO provides ongoing technical leadership on a part-time basis. The role can include technical strategy, architecture decisions, engineering priorities, hiring support, and responsibility for how a team builds and maintains software.
The scope depends on the company. The defining feature is continuing responsibility for technical direction.

toc.label: What does a fractional CTO do?
When is a different engagement more appropriate?
How does the role compare with other options?
How are fees and time commitments set?

whatTheyDo.title: What does a fractional CTO do?
body: A fractional CTO helps connect the company's goals to its technical decisions. That can mean choosing what to build, evaluating a platform, reviewing architecture, setting engineering priorities, or helping a founder understand the consequences of a technical choice.
Some engagements also include implementation. In my work, the balance between coding and leadership is defined around what the business needs.

whenYes.title: When does it make sense?
body: It can be useful when a company needs ongoing technical ownership but does not need a full-time executive. Examples include a founder carrying too many technical decisions, an engineering team without clear direction, or a product entering a stage that requires different architectural and organizational choices.

whenNo.title: When is a different engagement more appropriate?
body: A well-defined feature or integration may need a senior engineer. A discrete review may need a technical assessment. A role requiring full-time day-to-day ownership may need a full-time CTO or engineering leader.
Choose the engagement based on the responsibility and continuity required.

comparison.title: How does the role compare with other options?
rows: Architecture and implementation within an agreed area of responsibility
Analysis or delivery for a defined problem
Ongoing technical direction with a part-time commitment
Temporary ownership of the CTO role during a transition

fees.title: How are fees and time commitments set?
body: They depend on the scope, responsibility, and time required. For my engagements, we agree those details in a proposal after discussing the product and the support needed.
